To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the AT2 receptor polymorphism is associated with left ventricle structure in young hypertensive patients, and that the AT2 polymorphism is also associated with left ventricualr structure in patients with coronary artery disease and with the risk of MI in patients with hypertension.

the AT2 receptor polymorphism was not significantly associated with left ventricle mass index in the GLAEC and GLAOLD cohorts, but was associated with a higher incidence of cardiovascular events in the GLAOLD study.

a common biallelic intronic polymorphism of the AT2R gene (G+1675A) was associated with a number of cardiovascular phenotypes, including left ventricular mass, left ventricular mass relative to body surface area (LV mass index), and left ventricular posterior and septal thickness, as well in young hypertensive men, but not in normotensive men.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AT2 receptor gene polymorphisms are associated with cardiovascular phenotypes.
the AT2 receptor polymorphism G+ 1675A is associated with cardiovascular phenotypes in hypertensive males, and that this polymorphism is a candidate gene for left ventricular hypertrophy.
the G allele of the AT2R intron 1 polymorphism is a marker for a genetic susceptibility to left ventricular hypertrophy and cardiac remodeling in young hypertensive men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the A allele is associated with an increased left ventricular mass, and the A allele is also associated with an increased risk of developing MI.
AT2 gene polymorphism is associated with atherosclerotic disease and cardiovascular phenotypes in hypertensive subjects, and in particular in those with a family history of MI.
there is no clear evidence of an effect of the AT2 polymorphism G+1657A on the cardiovascular phenotypes investigated in this study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AT2R gene polymorphism is not related to the risk of MI in the elderly population.
the AT2 receptor G+1675 A polymorphism is associated with a higher prevalence of MI and a lower prevalence of hypertension in the general population.

the A allele of the bialleleic polymorphism G+1 675A in intron I of the AT2R gene is a marker for a more favourable cardiovascular phenotype in the general population, and in patients with hypertension and/or diabetes.
